proof_summary: For primes \(p,q\) with different last digits and \(pq\le150\), if neither divides \(d\), then \(d\) is invertible modulo \(pq\), so one of the first \(pq\) progression terms is divisible by both primes, a contradiction; hence \(p\mid d\) or \(q\mid d\). Applying this to selected pairs among \(2,3,5,7,11,13,17\) forces \(2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\mid d\) and then either \(11\mid d\) or \(13\mid d\), making \(2310\) or \(2730\) divide \(d\), contrary to \(d\le2025\).
